primitives.verbatim_quote: Shot-boundary detection is the first automated step: segment the broadcast into shots, then classify/rank the segments.

reasoning_traces.think:
Shot boundary detection operates on the principle of abrupt change in visual content, formalized through frame differencing. Let f(t) denote the intensity vector of frame at time t. A shot boundary occurs when Δf(t) exceeds a threshold τ, i.e., B(t) = 1 iff ||f(t) − f(t−1)|| > τ. This binary indicator is refined by a CNN classifier that learns to distinguish hard cuts from fades or dissolves. In GSE’s context, this becomes a temporal segmentation kernel K(t) = θ(Δf(t)) ⊗ ϕ(CNN(f(t))), where θ is a step function and ⊗ denotes convolution. The failure mode arises when gradual transitions are misclassified due to insufficient contrast or misalignment with CNN priors. Dualities emerge in that the same signal can be interpreted as either a scene cut or a camera movement depending on domain context. For GSI, this becomes a Bayesian update over shot likelihoods given frame evidence. For GSE, it defines a Markovian state space over broadcast time, where each shot represents a node in a directed graph of transitions.
